Design + build task in /opt/nxeon-staging (staging). Nxeon's marketing game-server landing pages (e.g. /minecraft-server-hosting, /rust-server-hosting, and 19 games via a shared `GameLandingPage` component) are considered by the owner to be stale, boring, generic, text-heavy, and off-putting. Your job: design and build **2–3 GENUINELY DISTINCT new visual directions** for the game-server landing template, as SAFE PREVIEW routes that do NOT touch any existing live page or the shared component. The owner will pick a direction; nothing ships from this task.

This owner has REJECTED generic AI design many times. Read `/root/.claude/projects/-root/memory/nxeon-marketing-design.md` in full first — it documents exactly what they reject and the real brand. Non-negotiables from it:

**The REAL brand (use these tokens, they exist in app/globals.css):** deep navy ground (`--color-navy-950 #060a14`, navy-900 #0a101f), violet brand (`--color-brand-500 #6f47f5`, brand-400 #8a70fb), blue/cyan accents (`--color-accent-blue #3b82f6`, `--color-accent-cyan #22d3ee`), glass cards, violet glow. Font is **Geist** (--font-sans). Reuse existing utility classes: `grad-text` (blue→violet gradient text), `.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.eyebrow`, `hero-aura`, `tone-panel/tone-deep/tone-light`, `.rail`. **Cyan is the "live/active" pop — NEVER use amber except as a semantic warning.**

**What they LIKE (evolve these, don't discard):** the glowing ambient background dots (`AmbientField`), gradient text (`grad-text`), the auto-sliding logo carousel (`LogoMarquee`), per-product/per-game accent colors, nav hover-underline, dropdown nav + icons, the speed message **"Your server is 47 seconds away"** (speed is their #1 buying trigger — lead with it), the interactive product SCREENS/animations, and they want MORE real screens/motion. Reusable showcase components live in `components/marketing/showcase/` — look at `GameControlPanel`, `ServerDashboard`, plus `DeployCard`, `MatrixTerminal`, `NetworkMap` (use NetworkMap for any map — NEVER a fake globe, they hate it).

**What they REJECT (do NOT produce):** the generic "AI slop" skeleton = a canvas particle field behind centered eyebrow → centered stacked headline → stat strip → 3-up feature-card grid → pricing → CTA. Every rejected version was that. Also: messy/dead-space "built for performance" feature cards, fake globes, generic rounded buttons (keep `.btn-primary`), walls of text. They explicitly want: **real game imagery as the centerpiece, asymmetric/editorial layouts (not centered-stack), striking motion that feels game-specific and premium, less text + more styling/presentation, beautiful icons, buying-psychology focus, and 5-star reviews on the page.**

**Real game art exists** — check `public/games/art/` for `<slug>_hero.jpg` and `<slug>_poster.jpg` (mapped in `GAME_ART_SLUG` in lib/games.ts). Pick 1–2 games with the richest existing art (Rust, Valheim, Palworld, ARK, Satisfactory typically have both hero + poster) and build the directions around that real art as the visual anchor — full-bleed hero art, parallax, art-derived accent color per game. Also `GameHero` / `GameCoverTile` components already handle the art resolution chain — study them.

### What to build
- 2–3 **distinct** new template directions (distinct LAYOUT CONCEPTS + distinct MOTION approaches, not 3 recolors of the same thing). Examples of genuinely different concepts to draw from (invent your own, don't just copy these): (a) a full-bleed cinematic game-art hero with an overlaid live-looking game control panel that animates (player count ticking, TPS graph), asymmetric split; (b) an editorial "magazine" layout — big art on one side, a vertical rail of numbered buying-reasons + a sticky animated plan card on the other; (c) a "command deck" concept — the game art framed inside a premium glass console UI with animated stat rails and a deploy terminal. Each must feel like a $50k agency landing page for THAT specific game, not a template.
- Each direction is a NET-NEW component (e.g. `components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCinematic.tsx`) rendered on a NET-NEW preview route (e.g. `app/(marketing)/preview/game-cinematic/page.tsx`, `.../game-editorial/page.tsx`, `.../game-console/page.tsx`). Do NOT edit `GameLandingPage`, any existing `*-server-hosting` page, or globals.css beyond ADDING new scoped classes/keyframes if needed.
- Real content for the chosen game (plans/slots/price can be realistic sample data pulled from an existing game's page so it looks real). Include the "47 seconds away" speed hook and a compact 5-star review element.
- Motion: use CSS/Framer-style transitions, scroll reveals, hover micro-interactions, an animated live-stats element — tasteful and premium, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`. NOT a generic particle canvas as the hero device.
- Mobile-responsive (a third of their traffic is mobile and converts poorly today — make these genuinely good on phones).

### Verify + capture
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (do NOT run `npm run build` — other agents are working; concurrent builds clobber .next). To capture screenshots, run the dev server on an alternate port (`PORT=3777 npm run dev` or similar) and use Playwright (it's available in this repo) to screenshot each preview route at desktop (1440w) AND mobile (390w) widths; save PNGs to /opt/nxeon-staging/.design-previews/ (create it). Shut the dev server down when done.
- Report back: the preview route paths, the game(s) you used, a 1-2 sentence description of each direction's concept + what makes it distinct, and the screenshot file paths. Be honest about anything that didn't render well.

Make these genuinely beautiful and distinct — this is the whole point of the task, and generic output will be rejected. Take real creative risks within the brand.

- **A — Cinematic Live-Ops (Rust):** full-bleed cinematic key-art hero, navy-scrimmed *asymmetric* split (headline + prominent "47 seconds away" hook on the left; a floating, genuinely-animated live server panel on the right — ticking player count, a drawn TPS graph, streaming console).
